lede: Democrats' sweep of both chambers of Congress sent the dollar and Treasury yields lower and oil sharply down, while the Dow posted its best post-midterm session in 44 years. Gold has pushed on to about $4,135 in Asia, and the Bank of England's expected first hike since 2023 is today's main event.
snapshot_time: Gold ≈06:50 TRT · Brent ≈05:00 TRT · FX & US500 = Wed 4 Nov close

focus.text: Building on Wednesday's ~3% jump, gold trades near $4,135 as the dollar and yields slip. It is now above the 20-day SMA (~$4,075); BoE at 15:00 and US jobless claims at 16:30 TRT are today's risks.
Closed Wednesday near 1.1232 after touching 1.1272, its best since early October, on a softer dollar and 4.0% eurozone inflation. German orders (10:00 TRT) and Friday's payrolls are next.

technicals.indicators: Daily RSI(14) ≈ 48 before the overnight push · 1h RSI ≈ 73 (overbought) · below 100-day SMA
technicals.note: The rebound from the 30 Oct low near $3,870 has cleared $4,000 and the late-October lower high at $4,082, with the 100-day SMA the next overhead marker.

technicals.indicators: Trading around the 4h 200-EMA · H4 momentum overbought · still below 100-day SMA
technicals.note: A short-term rising channel from late October carried price to a one-month high, but Wednesday's failure to hold 1.1270 left an upper wick.

technicals.indicators: H4 MACD above zero with rising signal line · H1 stochastic above 80
technicals.note: Sterling sits at a seven-week high into the BoE decision, with 1.3423 the first pullback zone inside the October–November recovery.

technicals.indicators: Fear & Greed 34 · back above STH cost basis and True Market Mean · ~36% below the $126k ATH
technicals.note: A short squeeze lifted bitcoin from $75,600 back above $80,000, but the sequence of lower highs since the summer peak is still in place.

technicals.indicators: Back above 200-day EMA · pressing 50-day EMA · +6.9% in 24h
technicals.note: Ether outpaced bitcoin and is testing its 50-day EMA from below after reclaiming the 200-day EMA.

news.text: Democrats now control both the House and Senate; Trump congratulated them but warned he would veto their agenda, setting up a divided Washington.
The Dow jumped 3% (about 1,570 points) and the S&P 500 1.6% to 7,688.62; energy lagged while Apple topped a $5T market value.
Brent lost nearly 8% Wednesday, falling under $100 for the first time since early October, and slipped toward $93.6 as Qatar circulated a US-Iran draft deal.
ISM services eased to 54.5 versus 54.8 expected while ADP payrolls rose 86k; the 10-year yield dipped to about 4.89%.
A quarter-point hike to 4% is almost fully priced for 15:00 TRT; Goldman expects a 7–2 vote and new forecasts may show inflation peaking in early 2027.
Bitcoin briefly touched about $81,000 as roughly $950M of leveraged positions were wiped out in 24 hours, most of them short bets.
US spot bitcoin ETFs saw a third day of outflows on Tuesday ($115.6M, IBIT −$95M), taking the three-day total near $1.16B; ether ETFs lost $85M.
Binance reopened withdrawals for several assets on Ethereum and BNB Chain after its security incident; CZ warned users about fake wallet sites.
ZEC rose about 7% as the NU7 upgrade, which cuts block times to 25 seconds, approaches activation around today.
On-chain data showed Trump Media moving about 4,259 BTC to Crypto.com.
About $275M of tokens across 12 projects unlock this week; Stable (STABLE) releases roughly $23M on Sunday.

upcoming.note: Hike to 4.00% almost fully priced; first increase since 2023.
Consensus +62k (prev +29k), unemployment 4.2%; key for December Fed hike odds.
Lower oil may temper the energy component; Fed hike pricing hinges on it.
Governor Karahan presents the year's final forecasts.
